cells.tense: You're here with it, hand on the work, and the draw is steady under you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're going toward, out loud, and take its next small step somewhere another person can see you do it. It shows you whether the draw holds once it leaves your head.
cells.core:
You can say what you're reaching toward, and the reach still moves you. The aim is reliable — it's there on a flat afternoon with nothing shining and it steers you without needing to be talked up. On a plain day you get up and take the next small step, and you don't have to remind yourself why. The direction is just there, doing its work.

You don't have to defend it or prove it to anyone. Let one visible step carry it forward, and what you're reaching toward becomes something you can stand on rather than haul around — and what you find out from taking that step stays yours, whatever comes of it.
cells.sheetLine: You know the direction and you are living inside it.
cells.verb: arriving at deep satisfaction with what you imagined, because you actually felt your way through it
cells.place: the part of you drawn toward what it is actually aiming at — a direction you recognize rather than one you were handed

cells.tense: You're out ahead of the thing, living in a version that hasn't happened.
cells.ask: Pick the goal that's furthest out and do only its next physical step this week — the call, the note, the page — leaving the rest alone each time the big picture flares up. It puts your energy where it can land.
cells.core:
There's something you're building, and on a good day you hold the next step and let the rest wait. That patience keeps the aim steady through a week that hands you nothing to show for it. You work; you let the picture stay a picture.

The vision has gotten loud enough that you keep living in its finished shape — rehearsing the outcome, imagining how it lands — so what you want runs ahead of the work. The bigness is real and it's yours; it just isn't a place to stand yet. Feed the one step and watch the pull get steadier instead of louder, and what you learn from that is yours.
cells.sheetLine: What you want has run out ahead of what you're doing.

cells.tense: Something stopped at a door you'd already walked through.
cells.ask: Once this week, take half an hour with no inputs and write one honest sentence about what you actually want — then leave it where you'll see it tomorrow. Nothing about it needs to be said to anyone else.
cells.core:
You have a pull toward something, and when it's working it shows up as a quiet knowing — you can name the direction without needing to act on it right away. That kind of knowing doesn't push. You notice what you want and you let that be enough for now; it stays yours and no one has to hear it.

The reach has gone quiet enough that you're standing behind it, past where the draw can get to you. Trying harder at wanting doesn't help. Give your own knowing room to form before anything has to be said about it, no performance, and what shows up in that room stays yours.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped somewhere past the thing you want and stayed there.

cells.tense: You're being pulled toward something and calling the pull weather.
cells.ask: Take one thing you're doing because you want to — a message, a page, a detour — and say to yourself, this is mine, this is what you're reaching for. Then let yourself notice you did it on purpose.
cells.core:
Your aiming runs on small daily choosing — you sit down with the thing on days you feel like it and days you don't, in a rhythm that stays mostly invisible. You turn toward what matters without making a show of it, and that's what keeps the direction real when nothing dramatic is happening.

The claim is absent, not the reach. You're already moving toward what you want and talking about it as if it happened to you, leaving the one doing the aiming out of their own story. Naming the reach as yours costs nothing and it tells you where you're actually headed.
